newsitem.title: UK: N Sea quiet as waits for news from OPEC and Iraq.
newsitem.headline: N Sea quiet as waits for news from OPEC and Iraq.

text.p: North Sea crude oil markets saw a slow start on Wednesday with traders focused on the OPEC meeting in Vienna amid news that Saudi Arabia and Iran were pushing the cartel's biggest quota violator, Venezuela, to cut excess production.
Although delegates at the meeting doubted this pressure would have much impact, traders said that if there was adherence to the quotas it would give the currently flagging market a boost.
"If we saw some indication that the quota busters were going to pull back (production) a bit the market would recover. For the moment it's very much a wait and see game," one said.

Although many traders were sceptical that Iraq would manage to start exporting crude in the next 10 days they said that if there were indications from the U.N. that this was possible the price of crude would fall sharply.

"Even at current prices we could see Iraq needing to export up to one million barrels of crude per day to make their money....and anyone who thinks this market can absorb that (in July) is out of their minds," one North Sea trader said.
Much of the pressure would come off in August though where a cut in North Sea production due to maintenance both in the U.K. and Norwegian sectors would be balanced by Iraqi exports.
August Brent on the IPE lost five cents to trade at $17.82 a barrel by 1201 GMT.
Iraq oil minister Amir Rasheed said on Tuesday said he expected his country to restart exporting up to 750,000 barrels of crude per day within 10 days.

North Sea sweet grades held steady with limited availabilities in the first two decades of July for many grades. Oseberg traded twice on Tuesday at dated Brent +15 cents. Traders saw other grades steady though limited supplies of Forties might see it tipping upwards in the next few days.

Intermonth spreads on the Brent lost ground with July/Aug and Aug/SEp talked around -20 cents. Similarly CFDs lost a few cents with next week offered at Aug -39 cents and the July 7-11 at Aug -38 cents.
